language gap G12 `[]const u8` slice holes: a STRING LITERAL lowered to a `[]const u8` slice value (ptr=static literal, len=byte count) read via `.len`+index, and a `[]mut u8`->`[]const u8` const-narrowing coercion (implicit let, call-arg, explicit `as`). Both backends must agree on the fat-pointer `{ptr,len}` slice repr

language gap G30 `*mut T`->`*const T`/`*T` single-pointer const-narrowing: passing a `*mut T` VALUE where an immutable pointer is expected is a safe no-op coercion (identical plain-pointer repr). Covers the coercion at a call arg, a `let` initializer, a return, and an explicit `as` cast; the REVERSE (const->mut) + element mismatch stay rejected. Both backends must agree

language gap G11 value optionals `?T` (`?u32`/`?usize`/`?Point`): a sized VALUE payload has no spare sentinel, so it lowers to a TAGGED aggregate `{present,value}` (C mc_opt_<T>; LLVM `{i1,T}`), distinct from the pointer nullables. Covers construction (present/absent null), `if let` narrowing, `== null`/`!= null` tag tests, `?` unwrap (trap on absent), returning `?T`, and passing `?T` by value. Both backends must agree on the tagged repr

language gap G18 generic tagged unions `union Opt<T> { some: T, none }`: a generic union is a template monomorphized per concrete use exactly like a generic struct — each `Opt<U>` becomes a distinct non-generic tagged union `Opt__U` (case payload `some: T` substituted to `some: U`), the generic decl dropped. Covers payload cases + payload-less cases (`none`, `ready`/`idle`), switch-binding typing the payload as the substituted type, type-generic constructors resolving against the concrete target, and two instantiations (`Opt<u32>`/`Opt<u64>`) producing distinct deduped concrete unions. Both backends must agree on the tagged repr

G20 block-scoped let/var: a local is scoped to its block, so a disjoint SIBLING block may reuse the name for a distinct binding (the original two-while-loop repro), while live-enclosing-shadow stays E_DUPLICATE_LOCAL. Exercises two while-body siblings reusing `t`, `{}`-block siblings reusing `t` at different types (u32/u64), sibling `for` element reuse, and nested-then-sibling reuse — folding distinct per-block values so a collapsed-storage lowering diverges on either backend

a local of POINTER type borrows its referent and does not own it: MIR resolved a local's owning type THROUGH the pointer, so `var p: *Token` was recorded as owning a `Token` and repointing it emitted a `reinit` on an already-live ownership root, failing the whole function with an internal InvalidMirOwnershipEvents. Takes a borrow of a move value, repoints it at a second, reads through both, and consumes each value exactly once. Both backends must agree

language gap G14 `&base.field`/`&base[i]` where `base` reaches storage THROUGH a pointer: the escape/move analysis must NOT flag it (the address points into pointed-to storage, not this frame's stack slot, so returning it does not dangle). Covers `&e.val` and `&e.arr[i]` through a pointer PARAMETER and `&p.val`, `&p.arr[i]`, `&p.inner.field`, plus a plain read and write of `p.val`, where `p` is a LOCAL holding a pointer copy; writes through each returned pointer and re-reads to confirm the alias. Both backends must agree

language gap G22 (§30 file-private name uniquification): two imported STRICT files each define a file-private `fn advance` with DIFFERENT signatures; the flattened unit no longer collides (E_DUPLICATE_DECLARATION) and each file's public entry binds to ITS OWN advance in both backends (a_step(3)=103, b_step(4,5)=27).
